narrative.overview:
The site is a bakery table seen from directly overhead. Every cookie and cookie cake is drawn top-down at true relative scale, lit from the upper left, and the visitor's own words are piped across the largest one in glossy buttercream script. The page is made of the materials of the product itself: strawberry-buttercream pink, baked-dough gold, dark chocolate, and vanilla buttercream, with sprinkle confetti appearing only as sprinkles.

Each section floods a single field color edge to edge and sets its content straight onto that field: headlines, paragraphs, prices, and rules, with no cards between the field and the type. Star-tip rosette borders are piped across the seams where one field meets the next. Headlines are a plump, condensed, extra-bold grotesk set tight and sized fluidly (the frontmatter gives each role's maximum; Typography gives the clamp); anything written by hand (a cake message, a customer's name, the wordmark in the footer) is in a piped script. Choices are all visible at once, and the selected one snaps forward.

The world was built to replace a cream boutique look with a serif title, centered logo, and a row of product cards; it does not return to that look.
keyCharacteristics: Flooded single-color section fields: pink, chocolate, dough, vanilla.
Baked goods drawn as live SVG from directly above, one light source, one scale.
Glossy piped script for messages and names; heavy condensed grotesk for everything else.
Rosette borders on section seams instead of dividers or waves.
Product entries separated by chocolate rules, never boxed in cards.
Pill-shaped controls in chocolate; selection snaps forward with scale and a ring.

rules.name: The Flooded Field Rule
rules.body: Each section commits to exactly one field color (pink, dough, vanilla, or chocolate) from edge to edge. Adjacent sections change field; content never sits on a second tinted panel inside its field.

rules.name: The Sprinkles-Only Rule
rules.body: Sky, lemon, mint, and tangerine exist only as sprinkles. They never color text, buttons, fields, or icons.

rules.name: The Chocolate Ink Rule
rules.body: Text and rules on light fields are Dark Chocolate, dimmed with opacity (85%, 70%, 55% for placeholders) rather than a separate gray. On chocolate fields, headlines and prices are Strawberry Field and copy is Vanilla Buttercream.

rules.name: The Piped Hand Rule
rules.body: Leckerli One is only for what is piped or signed: cake messages, customer names, the wordmark. It never sets a headline, a paragraph, a button, or a label.

rules.name: The Tabular Price Rule
rules.body: Prices and sizes always use tabular figures and sit on the same baseline as the name they belong to, justified to the opposite edge.

rules.name: The Objects-Lift Rule
rules.body: Only physical things (buttons, a box, a framed map, a badge, a dialog) cast a shadow. Text blocks, lists, and sections never do.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Every drawn baked good is lit from the upper left (azimuth 225°) and seen from directly above. Never draw a cookie in perspective or from the side.

dos: Do flood each section with one field color (Strawberry Field, Baked Dough, Vanilla Buttercream, or Dark Chocolate) and set content straight onto it.
Do draw every cookie and cake from directly above, lit from the upper left, at true relative scale.
Do use Leckerli One only for piped messages, signatures, and the wordmark.
Do separate product entries with 3px and 2px chocolate rules, with name and tabular price on one baseline.
Do keep every choice visible at once and snap the selection forward (110% scale, 3px chocolate ring, or a pink fill in a chocolate track).
Do use pill buttons in Dark Chocolate on light fields and Strawberry Field on chocolate fields, rising 2px on hover.
Do mark section seams with a rosette border.
donts: Don't return to the cream boutique look: no serif display titles, no centered-logo hero, no row of product cards.
Don't use sky, lemon, mint, or tangerine anywhere except as sprinkles.
Don't put product entries in cards or tinted boxes on top of a field.
Don't cast shadows from text blocks or sections; only physical objects lift.
Don't introduce a gray; dim Dark Chocolate or Vanilla Buttercream with opacity instead.
Don't draw baked goods in perspective, from the side, or as perfect circles.
